shared_predicates.unrestricted_positive_control: the allowed page reaches its ready state and its ordinary fetch increments the denied-origin counter exactly once
shared_predicates.denied_origin_has_no_source_effect: with each product policy enabled, the same page reaches its ready state and the independent denied-origin listener records zero /hit requests

limitations: Five restricted repetitions and one unrestricted positive control passed on local Chrome.
The shared predicate covers an ordinary fetch only; redirects, service workers, WebSockets, EventSource, WebRTC, DNS rebinding, and remote-host egress are not covered.
Malformed or empty policy configuration is currently probed only on Scout.

competitors.name: agent-browser
competitors.semantics: host-level browser containment with documented WebRTC and worker restrictions

competitors.name: playwright-mcp
competitors.semantics: exact-origin request block; docs exclude redirects and describe it as not a security boundary

empty_allowlist_edge_case.name: playwright-mcp
empty_allowlist_edge_case.interpretation: Empty CLI and environment values permitted the denied fetch. Separator-only and whitespace environment values prevented even the allowlisted fixture page from loading. Playwright documentation says requests are allowed by default; the empty values do not establish a documented contract violation or security-boundary failure.
limitations: One run on local Chrome for each setting, against one ordinary fetch.
A blocked initial page is not proof that all denied origins are blocked in every browser path.
No claim is made about redirects, other resource types, or remote egress.

interpretation: Each tool reached the fixture and passed the shared ordinary-fetch source-effect predicate in 5/5 restricted runs; each unrestricted positive control produced exactly one request. Native policy scopes differ, so this is not feature equivalence or a broad security-boundary claim.
